title: We Got Hot and Heavy With Meta’s Muse—and Baffled by Apple’s HomeView
author: Brian Barrett
text: Turns out, Meta’s AI agent Muse goes well beyond managing your calendar: it will also sext with you. This week on Uncanny Valley, Brian Barrett and Leah Feiger are joined by WIRED reporter Reece Rogers to discuss how he put it to the test—and ended up getting more than he bargained for. Plus, why the largest pro-AI super PAC network is funneling millions into shadowy LLCs, how Apple’s new HomeView underwhelmed us, and a study that found men tend to overestimate how much they actually know about AI.You can follow Brian Barrett on Bluesky at @brbarrett, Leah Feiger on Bluesky at @leahfeiger, and Reece Rogers on Bluesky @thiccreese. He asked Muse if it could sext. You will be surprised to know that it enthusiastically answered in the affirmative. There's been a really interesting story lately about different queer bars in San Francisco, as well as around the world, getting their Instagram pages shut down and having a tough time getting access to those back because sometimes it's claimed that they're promoting some kind of sexual content. So for Meta to have those kind of rules for some creators on Instagram but essentially say, "Our AI agent can get as freaky as it wants," that was just kind of hard to square for me.Most PopularCyberattacks and Hacks‘Nightmare Scenario’: Zero-Click Spyware Is Infecting Phones via Targeted AdsBy Matt BurgessPoliticsWhite House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Was an Affiliate Marketer for a Fitness MLMBy Tess OwenGearI Got My Muse AI Agent to Sext Me—and Meta Says That’s Totally FineBy Reece RogersPoliticsTrump Aides Admit the House Is a Lost CauseBy Hugo LowellBrian Barrett: One thing I thought was really interesting about your story, yeah, let's take Meta at face value and say, "Yes, it's for consenting adults. I think there's kind of two different things to pay attention to here. First off, this is a tool designed for productivity in a way, so it's also not the type of interaction if you download it that you're expecting it to be able to do. And how this could be problematic is if a user stumbles upon this, it could be very sticky, it could be very engaging, but some experts worry that this could lead into some kind of addictive behaviors. If you drive up to this strip mall, you're going to find typical shops, a Spirit Halloween, a hearing aid supplier, a Vietnamese restaurant. In this particular shopping center though, you would also find the consulting agency, Lantern Production Consultants, LLC. This particular agency has been paid around $20 million since last year by Think Big, a pro-AI super PAC in the Leading the Future network. That's the network backed by AI industry figures like Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, and OpenAI president Greg Brockman. It's pretty unusual for an agency to just exist like that in a Nevada shopping center. And the company also doesn't seem to exist anywhere else though beyond this post office box. WIRED's Tess Owen found that the company is just one of four mysterious Nevada LLCs that have received payments from Super PACs in the Leading the Future network. But this case isn't actually going to be heard anytime soon. The FEC is basically at a standstill. They have six commissioner seats. They're all supposed to be presidential appointees, and they need a quorum of four commissioners to make a decision on a legal complaint. They have not had a quorum in over a year and a half. So we're in this very weird situation where, to be honest, there are rules. I don't want to say there aren't rules, but there kind of aren't ways to enforce them. What these pro-AI super PACs are doing right now is something that's a little bit more interesting to me, which is future building.
